The story of Mary and Martha — two sisters who welcome Jesus into their home, and what unfolds reveals a timeless truth about what it means to truly sit in God's presence.

The story of the woman at the well — a Samaritan woman with a complicated past meets Jesus alone at a well in the middle of the day, and a simple conversation about water becomes one of the most profound moments of grace and recognition in all of Scripture.

The story of the Transfiguration — Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain, where his appearance is transformed in dazzling light, Moses and Elijah appear beside him, and the disciples hear the voice of God, leaving them overwhelmed and forever changed.
The story of the Widow's Offering — a poor woman quietly drops two small coins into the temple treasury, and Jesus tells his disciples that she has given more than all the wealthy donors combined.

The story of Zacchaeus — a despised tax collector who climbs a tree just to catch a glimpse of Jesus, and finds himself not only seen but personally invited into a life-changing encounter that transforms him completely.
The story of Abraham and Isaac on Mount Moriah — a father asked to give up what he loves most, who trusts God completely, and discovers that God himself provides at the very moment of surrender.
The story of Elijah under the juniper tree — a burnt-out prophet who wanted to give up, and the tender, unexpected way God met him in his exhaustion.

The Parable of the Prodigal Son — a young man demands his inheritance early, wastes it all, and hits rock bottom, yet when he finally turns back toward home, his father is already running to meet him with open arms.
The story of Joseph — sold into slavery by his own brothers, falsely imprisoned, and forgotten, yet rising to save nations and ultimately forgiving the very people who betrayed him.

The story of Daniel in the lions' den — a man of quiet, unshakeable faith who kept praying when it became illegal, was thrown to the lions, and walked out untouched the next morning, leaving a king and a kingdom in awe of God.

The story of the Road to Emmaus — two discouraged disciples walking away from Jerusalem after the crucifixion encounter a mysterious stranger who opens the Scriptures to them, and only recognize him as the risen Jesus in the breaking of bread.

The story of David and Goliath — a young shepherd boy steps onto a battlefield to face a towering warrior that every trained soldier was too afraid to fight, armed with nothing but a sling, five stones, and an unshakeable trust in God.

Ruth, a foreign widow, leaves everything she knows to stay loyal to her mother-in-law Naomi, and her faithfulness leads her into a life of blessing, belonging, and redemption she never could have planned.

The Parable of the Good Samaritan — a man left for dead on a dangerous road, two respected religious figures who pass him by, and an unlikely stranger who stops to show extraordinary, costly compassion.
The story of Esther — a young Jewish woman placed in an unlikely position of power who risks her life to save her entire people, discovering that she may have been prepared for exactly this moment.

The story of Jonah — a prophet who ran from God's call, was swallowed by a great fish, and discovered that God's mercy pursues us even when we flee from it, and extends even to those we'd rather not forgive.

Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue and are thrown into a furnace so hot it kills the soldiers who throw them in — yet they walk out unharmed, and a mysterious fourth figure is seen walking beside them in the flames.
The story of the Feeding of the Five Thousand — a vast hungry crowd, a boy's small lunch, and how Jesus takes what seems laughably insufficient and multiplies it into abundance for thousands.

The story of Lazarus — Jesus receives word that his dear friend is gravely ill, arrives four days after Lazarus has died, and raises him from the tomb, revealing himself as the resurrection and the life.

The story of the Burning Bush — Moses, a shepherd in exile tending his flock on a quiet mountain, encounters God in a flame that does not consume, and is called to a mission far greater than anything he felt capable of.
The story of Noah — a man who trusted God's word, built an ark when there was no sign of rain, and witnessed both the devastation of a flood and the tender promise of a rainbow on the other side.

The story of Gideon — a man who saw himself as the least of the least, yet was called by God to lead a great deliverance, and learned that victory doesn't depend on strength in numbers but on trust in God.

The story of the Paralyzed Man Lowered Through the Roof — four devoted friends carry a paralyzed man to Jesus, and when the crowd blocks every entrance, they refuse to give up, cutting a hole in the roof to lower him down.

The story of the Transfiguration — Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain, where he is suddenly transformed before their eyes in dazzling light, and Moses and Elijah appear beside him, before a voice from a cloud declares him God's beloved Son.
The story of the Wedding at Cana — Jesus performs his first recorded miracle by turning water into wine at a wedding feast, revealing his glory in a quiet, unexpected, and deeply human moment.

The story of the woman at the well — a Samaritan woman with a complicated past has an unexpected, life-changing conversation with Jesus at a well in the middle of the day, and discovers that she is fully known, fully accepted, and offered living water that will never run dry.
The story of the Ten Lepers — ten men healed by Jesus, but only one turns back to give thanks, and that one act of gratitude changes everything about what it means to be truly made whole.
The story of Elijah under the juniper tree — a burnt-out prophet who wanted to give up, and the quiet, gentle way God met him not with thunder or fire, but with rest, food, and a still small voice.

The Prodigal Son — a young man who demands his inheritance early, wastes it all, and in his lowest moment turns back toward home, only to find a father already running to meet him with arms wide open.

Joseph is sold into slavery by his own brothers, suffers unjust imprisonment, yet rises to save nations — and ultimately forgives the very people who betrayed him, because he sees God's hand in the whole journey.

The story of Daniel in the lions' den — a man of deep faith who refused to stop praying even when it was made a crime, and who was delivered from certain death in a way that left a king and a kingdom in awe.

The story of the Prodigal Son's older brother — a faithful son who never left, yet struggled to celebrate his brother's return, and what Jesus reveals about the danger of a heart that obeys but quietly resents.

The story of David and Goliath — a young shepherd boy steps onto a battlefield to face a towering warrior that an entire army was too afraid to fight, armed with nothing but a sling, five stones, and an unshakeable trust in God.
Ruth leaves everything she has ever known to stay beside her grieving mother-in-law Naomi, and her quiet faithfulness leads her — and a broken family — to unexpected restoration and belonging.

The story of the Good Samaritan — a traveler left for dead on a dangerous road, two religious men who pass by without helping, and an unlikely stranger who stops, kneels down, and shows what loving your neighbor actually looks like.

Peter walks on water toward Jesus in the middle of a stormy night — and what happens when his eyes drift from Jesus to the waves reveals something profound about faith, fear, and being caught before you sink.

The story of Queen Esther — a young Jewish woman who rose to royalty in a foreign land, and when her people faced destruction, found the courage to risk everything by stepping forward and saying, "If I perish, I perish."

The story of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego — three young men who refused to bow to a golden idol, were thrown into a furnace so hot it killed the soldiers who threw them in, and walked out unharmed, with a mysterious fourth figure seen walking beside them in the flames.
The story of Jonah — a prophet who ran from God's call, was swallowed by a great fish, and discovered that there is no direction you can run that puts you beyond God's reach or God's mercy.
Mary of Bethany anoints Jesus with costly perfume, and what looks like a wasteful act turns out to be one of the most beautiful and profound gestures of devotion in the entire Gospel.

The story of the Road to Emmaus — two grieving disciples walk away from Jerusalem after the crucifixion, not recognizing that the risen Jesus himself has joined them on the road, and how their hearts burn within them before their eyes are finally opened.
The story of Zacchaeus — a despised tax collector who climbed a tree just to catch a glimpse of Jesus, and found that Jesus had already seen him, chosen him, and was ready to change his life forever.

The story of Gideon — a man who saw himself as the least of the least, yet was called by God to lead Israel to victory against overwhelming odds, learning that true strength comes not from numbers or confidence, but from God alone.

The story of Noah — a man who trusted God's word and built an ark while the world around him saw nothing but clear skies, and how faithful obedience in the unseen prepared the way for rescue and a brand-new beginning.

The story of the Feeding of the Five Thousand — a massive hungry crowd, one boy's small lunch, and how Jesus took what seemed laughably insufficient and multiplied it into more than enough for everyone.

The story of Lazarus — Jesus arrives four days after his dear friend has died, and what unfolds at the tomb reveals something about grief, faith, and the power of the one who calls himself the resurrection and the life.
The story of the Tower of Babel — a humanity united in pride that tried to build its way to heaven, and how God's response reshaped the entire world.
The story of the Widow's Offering — a poor woman drops two tiny coins into the temple treasury, and Jesus tells his disciples that she has given more than all the wealthy donors combined.

The story of the Burning Bush — Moses, a fugitive shepherd in the wilderness, encounters God in a flame that does not consume, and is called back to face everything he ran from, armed with nothing but a promise.

The story of the Paralyzed Man at the Pool of Bethesda — a man who had been unable to walk for thirty-eight years encounters Jesus, who asks him a surprisingly personal question and then does the unexpected.

The story of Joseph — a favored son sold into slavery by his own brothers, who endures betrayal, false accusation, and years in prison, yet rises to save the very people who wronged him, revealing how God can weave suffering into purpose.
Elijah, exhausted and convinced he is utterly alone after fleeing for his life, is met by God not in thunder or fire, but in a gentle whisper — and is tenderly restored and recommissioned.
The Prodigal Son — a young man who demands his inheritance early, wastes it all, and finally comes to his senses and returns home, only to be met by a father who was already running toward him.
David, a young shepherd boy armed with nothing but a sling and unwavering faith, steps forward to face the giant Goliath when every trained soldier in Israel has backed away in fear.
The story of Daniel in the lions' den — a man of unwavering prayer who refused to hide his faith even when a death sentence hung over him, and how God shut the mouths of the lions.
The story of Ruth — a young Moabite widow who chose loyalty over security, followed her mother-in-law into a foreign land, and discovered that faithful love is never wasted or unseen.
The story of the Good Samaritan — a parable Jesus told about a man left for dead on a dangerous road, and the unlikely stranger who stopped to help him when everyone else walked by.
The story of Esther — a young Jewish woman who found herself queen of Persia at just the right moment, and had to decide whether to risk everything to save her people from destruction.

The story of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego — three young men who refused to bow to a king's golden idol and were thrown into a blazing furnace, only for a mysterious fourth figure to appear walking beside them in the flames.
The story of Jonah — a prophet who ran in the opposite direction from God's call, discovered there is no outrunning divine purpose, and learned that God's mercy reaches further than any of us expect.
